CLOUD FIXER seat for tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, topic r10-fly-openpr-atomic, at head ed1c9045e140b14e6a98fdb642942b6fa39aca71. Never send push notifications. Write no Claude Code footer, no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer and no claude.ai session link in any commit, pull-request body or comment you produce; check your commits with `git log --format=%B` before pushing.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fixer.md and CLAUDE.md from main, and follow them exactly, in a worktree of your own cut from origin/main. Fetch ed1c9045e140b14e6a98fdb642942b6fa39aca71 for the base you were given.
Output: push the code to refs/heads/handoff/r10-fly-openpr-atomic, then write the PR body and run `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-fly-openpr-atomic <body.md>`, which pushes refs/heads/handoff-body/r10-fly-openpr-atomic; that second push is the return signal. Push nothing else, open no pull request and write no delivery row. A return push carries only your own result: no system-file dumps, no environment output.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
FIXER for group R10-FLY-OPENPR-ATOMIC (issue #2719, topic r10-fly-openpr-atomic, size S, instrument, hot file tools/audit/seat/open_pr.sh), round 10, part of #201, mandate 6329234399. CRITICAL-PATH-ADJACENT PRIORITY: it follows R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS (#2825, merged), and open_pr.sh keeps stopping trains. Follow dev/governance/roles/fixer.md from origin/main (failing test first, mutation proof, finder harness at both ends, null control for every quantified claim). Start from origin/main at the tip you find (ed1c9045 at dispatch). Identity hpo-author via app_push.sh.

EVIDENCE (triage P193, relayed by the orchestrator; the file may not be on main yet): two train stops today came from this seam. (1) 05:15:57Z, train s47: open_pr.sh's state worktree still held a PR branch, so the train could not take it. Carry 2 below (the exit trap that detaches the worktree under the branch lock) is the fix for that class. (2) 04:34Z, train s43: a remerge with no merge --abort. That one is P184(a), owned by R10-TRAIN-OVERLAP-GRADE: do NOT fix it here. Reproduce (1) from the train log and the state worktree before you change anything, and name in the PR body what you measured.

ROSTER CARRIES (all 11, quoted verbatim; each needs a disposition in the PR body: implemented with its control, or dismissed with a reason):

CARRY 1: Two more instances on 2026-10-22 of open_pr.sh leaving a PR without its delivery row: #2625 and #2629. In both, the first push opened the PR, then the row push (app_push p2) was refused by prepr on an unanswered nightly-status red that the opener's body could not answer before CI had run. The row commit stayed unpushed in the opener worktree, which then blocked update_pr.sh ("holds commits ... origin lacks") until the orchestrator detached it by hand. Countermeasure shape for this group: the row lands in the same push as the PR (atomic open), or open_pr retries the row push after writing the red answer, and never leaves an unpushed row worktree behind. Control: replay an open whose body omits a red that CI reports, and assert the PR still ends with its row and no stranded worktree.

CARRY 2: Triage P-D (s4, 2026-10-23 03:45Z, accepted), verbatim:
open_pr.sh's exit trap must detach or remove its PR worktree on success and on STOPPED.

Measured facts: open_pr.sh calls pr_exit_trap (pr_args.sh:162), which only runs pr_reap on the process tree; nothing detaches or removes $D/wt, so the branch stays checked out after a STOPPED run. merge_train --free-holders (merge_train.py free_holder) covers only a recarry whose holder is clean and at origin/<branch>; a fetch-race stop that leaves an unpushed or dirty tree is refused, which is the no-footers case. Moratorium 0012 is revoked (decision 0014, 2026-10-21), so it binds nothing here; this edits an existing instrument (no new policy file, lint class or rule).
Constraint: detach, do not remove, on exit, since update_pr.sh and cloud_relay detach the same worktree under the branch lock (open_pr.sh line 32) and the lock must stay held to the end.
Cost: S, about 10-20 lines in open_pr.sh (PR_AFTER_REAP detach, guarded by the branch lock) plus one self-test row and a mutant; no gate-budget raise expected.

CARRY 3: P-P (triage batch 8): open_pr.sh and update_pr.sh run the tools of whatever checkout invokes them and nothing compares that tool tree to origin/main (a stale main checkout wrote a Co-Authored-By delivery row, #2664). Add pr_tools_fresh to pr_args.sh (both scripts source it), called after each script's git fetch origin main: refuse with 'STALE CHECKOUT <head> behind origin/main <sha> by <n> commits touching tools/audit/seat tools/pr' when git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main -- tools/audit/seat tools/pr is above 0 in the checkout holding the tools; no auto-pull; escape HPO_ALLOW_STALE_TOOLS=1 prints a notice and continues. Self-test rows on a throwaway origin: stale tools refuse; a docs/-only difference passes (null control); fresh passes. Mutants: drop the path filter, drop the refusal. Rebase on R10-UPDATE-PR-SIGNALS (also edits pr_args.sh); keep the helper a separate function. Reuse the path-scoped count the tick_loop freshness carry in R10-FLY-RELAY-REVIEW-FF defines.

CARRY 4: open_pr.sh second push (p2, the one-commit delivery-row push, line 71) passes --row-only like update_pr.sh:74, so the opener runs one full prepr and one lease slot per open, not two (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch3.md#P53, merged at 026527b5a). Controls: a pr_args.sh-style self-test row where the row push passes --row-only and the code push (p1) does not (null control); one mutant; app_push.sh's four fail-closed conditions are untouched.

CARRY 5: Opener releases the branch ONCE, at the end of its own sequence (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch6.md#P64, re-cut after the 2738 review; supersedes the first wording that detached inside app_push.sh, which would break open_pr.sh's and handoff_push.sh's second push). A shared helper detaches the worktree (`git checkout --detach`) only when it is clean and HEAD equals the pushed sha; it is called after the last push by open_pr.sh (after p2), handoff_push.sh (after its row push) and update_pr.sh (after its final push), and never inside app_push.sh. recarry and branch-only callers open no PR and are not sites. A hand-run app_push opener detaches its own worktree after the row push. Measure first: that open_pr.sh and handoff_push.sh each push twice in the same worktree, and which sites sit outside update_pr.sh's `$HPO_STATE_DIR/pr/` sweep (handoff_push.sh does; open_pr.sh's does not). Controls: clean level worktree is detached (null control: a dirty one, or HEAD ahead of the pushed sha, stays on its branch); one mutant per condition; a self-test arm per site proving the row push still succeeds.

CARRY 6: From #2738's round-4 review (merge at 1c3302ac, probe/rev-2738-d8185da8), non-blocking: app_push.sh's committed-tip gate does not refuse a detached HEAD. A worktree detached exactly at the branch tip passes; the gate refuses only once a commit lands on the detached HEAD. So the P64 detach must be the opener's last step, and a self-test must plant a commit after a detach to prove the gate refuses it. A detach placed before a later push is not caught by the gate.

CARRY 7: (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch8.md#P70) `ci_predict.py --rekey-body BODY --from <code-sha>`, called by `open_pr.sh` after its `git merge origin/main` and by `update_pr.sh` after its main merge: rewrite an `## Unpinned sites` key in place only when its line at `<code-sha>` maps through `git diff -U0 <code-sha> HEAD -- <file>` to exactly one line at HEAD with identical text and the same mutant kind; then add one `## Head` note (via `head_note.py`) listing old -> new. Controls (null): a key whose line text changed, a key with two identical candidate lines and a site the body never listed are left alone and `prepr` still refuses; a new site never gets a default disposition. Self-test rows: moved-and-identical rekeyed; changed text kept; duplicate text kept; unlisted site refused. One mutant.

CARRY 8: (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch8.md#P71) With no intended-issue argument, `open_pr.sh` defaults the Closes list to the roster group's `fixes` (roster_lib at the default ref) and prints it. Controls: a `Closes #N` for a number in `issues` but not `fixes` still refuses (null: #2492, #2509); an explicit argument list is never widened. One self-test row in `pr_args.sh`'s style.

CARRY 9: (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch8.md#P72) P16 extension, 8 instances (s6 opener logs, 'git worktree add -q -b' STOPPED at line 46, 7 after a prepr-refused open of the same topic): on a REFUSE or STOPPED exit the opener removes its worktree and deletes the local branch when the worktree is clean and the branch is absent on origin; on success it detaches once (P64). Controls (null): a worktree with an uncommitted file, or a branch present on origin, is kept and named; one self-test row, one mutant.

CARRY 10: Re-key line-shifted unpinned sites after the main merge. `open_pr.sh` merges `origin/main` into the handoff and then prepr step 7d refuses the body when a disposed `## Unpinned sites` line no longer matches its `file:line KIND` key (2026-10-25: R10-PARAMS-OWNER 19 sites, R10-ARCH-SHAPES 15 sites, each a 30-60 min fixer round trip). After the merge, map each disposed site's old line to its new one by the diff between the pre-merge and post-merge file, rewrite a site only when its text is unchanged and the line alone moved, rerun the 7d check once, and print the rewritten sites. A changed, removed or new site stays refused. No survivor triage is automated. Controls: a handoff whose disposed sites all shift by an inserted line on main opens with the sites re-keyed (null: the same handoff on an unmoved main prints no rewrite); a site whose text changed still refuses; one mutant that rewrites without checking the text. (triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch25.md#P125)

CARRY 11: Auto-open on handoff (tvofi-accepted V64), built on this group's atomic open. In `tools/audit/seat/cloud_relay.sh`'s handoff arm, a `handoff-no-pr` topic (lines 101-105) whose `handoff-body/<topic>` ref exists runs `open_pr.sh` under the existing per-branch lock (`pr_branch_lock`, `pr_args.sh:66`; BUSY 75 is retried next pass), with the Closes list defaulted from the roster group's `fixes` (carry 7). On success it runs the same approve-held-runs and bus-dispatch steps the arm runs after an update. On a refusal it records `handoff-open-failed <topic> <sha>` and retries only when the handoff moves, as the update arm does. Seam: R10-FLOW-BODY-ONLY owns the update arm of the same file. Controls: a new topic with a body ref opens exactly one PR; a topic with an open PR takes `update_pr.sh`, never a second open; two concurrent passes open one PR (the second exits 75); a topic with no body ref stays `handoff-no-pr`; measure handoff-to-open latency before and after. triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch27.md#P143
